fit.verdict: The best-matched of the four roles, and it keeps getting stronger as the real body of work surfaces. Leroy is a practicing tax preparer who builds accounting software: Well (a PUBLISHED Chrome Web Store product that automates supplier-invoice retrieval into QuickBooks/Xero — i.e. Mercury's literal problem statement), ReconcileIQ (an account-reconciliation app with real clients incl. a Form 990 nonprofit), and TaxesByRoss (the platform behind his own tax practice). Plus TOBA (a live 501(c)(3) platform build where he runs a monthly cadence with a board member and has pitched a seven-committee consolidation vision to the full board), InsureBridge, and Titan Couriers. All five are now built as structured case studies on the Paintbrush /use-cases page — each in its own visual language, with real logos and brand colors and a geometrically-accurate device frame. The remaining gap: the case-study screens are still coded skeletons with REPLACE markers rather than real product screenshots, there is no written decision log / brief yet, and collaboration has been design + stakeholders rather than design + PM + eng + research.

criteria.name: 6+ yrs leading complex, end-to-end product design initiatives
criteria.note: 10+ yrs, 'Product Designer & Partner', and a deep bench of shipped products — Well (published), ReconcileIQ, TaxesByRoss, TOBA (multi-surface, board stakeholders), InsureBridge, Titan. No engineering partner or formal research is what keeps it at 8, not 9.

criteria.name: Thinks in systems & workflows, not screens
criteria.note: Data-driven architecture, Style Registry governance, the TOBA permissions model, Well's self-healing workflow blueprints and multi-format export system.

criteria.name: Learns new domains obsessively until can challenge experts
criteria.note: He doesn't learn accounting — he has run a private tax practice since 2015 (150+ clients), prepares Form 990 filings on contract for Trydent Advisors (Tallahassee), and built both his practice software (TaxesByRoss) and a published invoice-automation product (Well). Domain operator, not learner.

criteria.name: Turning highly complex workflows into simple experiences
criteria.note: Well's whole shipped pitch is 'days of clicking and chasing invoices -> one click'. Plus ReconcileIQ, courier dispatch, checkout, admin intake.

criteria.name: Balances automation with transparency, trust, user control
criteria.note: 'Human-approved, never auto-sends' agents; TOBA audit trail; Well's invoice-data validation, an AI receipt-fraud detector, and 'no passwords stored, GDPR/CCPA'.

criteria.name: Product judgment, clear communication, high ownership
criteria.note: TOBA is a real record here: he redirected the project from 'random information' to systematic feature-by-feature building (judgment under ambiguity), runs a monthly cadence with his committee-lead board member, and has presented the product to the full board — pitching a consolidation vision (seven committees' information into one system) and how it changes the organization's workflow. That is recurring product communication to a governing body, and they are funding the build, so the pitch landed. Held at 7, not 8-9: it is verbal + live-demo to a volunteer nonprofit board, not written docs/decks to PM + eng + exec, and there is still no decision log or brief a hiring manager can read.

criteria.name: Uses AI to accelerate exploration without compromising craft
criteria.note: Provider routing, fine-tuning, explicit 'where AI does not belong' rules — and Well is an AI-native accounting product (extractor, fraud detector, receipt generator).

criteria.name: Polished UI craft
criteria.note: Well, ReconcileIQ, TaxesByRoss, InsureBridge, TOBA are all real product UI, and each now has a structured case study on /use-cases in its own visual language with real logos and brand colors — up from folder names / a Chrome listing / one-line cards. Still short of 8-9 until real product screenshots replace the coded skeleton screens. Kraken is a branding project, not product UI.

strengths: Well — a PUBLISHED, publicly verifiable product that solves Mercury's exact stated problem (invoice/transaction data -> the books), AI-native
Practicing tax preparer since 2015 (150+ clients; contract 990 work for Trydent Advisors, Tallahassee) who builds his own accounting software — a domain operator, not a domain learner

TOBA: a current multi-surface platform build for a real 501(c)(3), board as product stakeholders, hard compliance constraints — with a monthly board-member cadence and full-board product presentations pitching a seven-committee consolidation vision
Automation-with-trust baked in — validation, fraud detection, audit trails, human-in-the-loop agents
Strongest AI-in-craft story of any applicant tier
Title and tenure support the 'product designer' claim
gaps: No engineering partner or formal user research on any project — collaboration is design + stakeholders/clients (incl. a real monthly board cadence and full-board product pitches at TOBA), not design + PM + eng + research inside a product org
Evidence is overwhelming in substance but exists only as code / folders / a Chrome listing — zero design case studies with flows, screens, and a visible craft pass
No written artifact that demonstrates product judgment — a decision log or product brief

improvementPlan.summary: The score is solidly apply-range (~8.0, up from ~7.5). Every move here is packaging, not new work. STATUS (2026-09-09): all five product case studies are now built as structured skeletons on the Paintbrush /use-cases 'Product & Platforms' track — Well, ReconcileIQ + TaxesByRoss, TOBA, InsureBridge, Titan Couriers — each in its own visual language, with a real-asset pass done (real logos, real brand colors, a geometrically-accurate iPhone frame on Titan). That lifted Polished UI craft 6 → 7 (7.5 → 7.8); surfacing the TOBA board cadence + full-board product pitches lifted Product judgment / communication 6 → 7 (7.8 → 8.0). Remaining: drop real product screenshots into the REPLACE markers (→ craft 8-9), and write the one-page decision log / brief (→ communication 8, and the first written artifact a hiring manager can read). Fully executed, ~8.7.
